title: Join a shelf to a cabinet side with cam locks: cams open to the edge, push the shelf on, turn them tight
instruction: Join the shelf to the cabinet side with its two cam locks.
context: Assembling flat-pack furniture at home is one of the most familiar practical jobs: bookcases, wardrobes and kitchen units arrive as panels joined by cam-and-bolt connectors, a bolt in one panel and a cam in a bore in the other's face. The instructions show the first step: turn each cam's opening to the edge (its arrow at the bolt) before the panels go together, or the bolt's head meets the cam's side and the panel will not go on. Turned half a round clockwise, the cam then draws the joint shut.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. Fixed: a 16 mm white melamine particleboard cabinet side (32 x 12 cm) standing upright in a steel jig, its face at x 40, along y from -16 to 16; two Minifix-type connecting bolts for drilling distance 24 mm (M6 thread, 10 mm heads) about 25 mm out of its face at y -9 and 9, 8 mm up, and two 8 mm beech dowels 12 mm out at y -11.5 and 11.5. Loose: a 16 mm white melamine shelf (20 x 26 cm, 0.5 kg) lying flat at x 17 to 37, y -13 to 13, its edge 3 cm from the side's face; in its top face two 15 mm zinc cam housings in 15 mm bores, their middles 2.4 cm in from that edge (drilling distance B = 24 mm) at y -9 and 9, their arrows pointing to -y (right) and +y (left), a quarter turn from the edge. Two PH2 x 100 screwdrivers (0.12 kg; red and yellow 28 mm handles) stand in wooden holders (4 x 4 x 3 cm, 9 mm hole) at x 24, y -20 and 20.
scoring: Measured at the end by looking at the joint and the holders, with a feeler gauge at the joint. 1.0 if both cams are locked (turned at least 120 degrees clockwise past open with the bolt's head in them), the joint is shut at both bolts (gap at most 0.5 mm), both screwdrivers stand back in their holders, and no part of either gripper is within 1 cm of the shelf or the screwdrivers, all still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s; 0.5 if the joint is locked and shut but not as for 1.0; 0.25 if both bolts' heads are in their cams but the joint is not locked and shut; else 0 (for example the shelf pushed onto a cam still closed, which stops it 9 mm short).
reset_notes: Turn the cams back half a round, pull the shelf off, turn the cams to the starting marks, lay the shelf at its mark and stand the screwdrivers in their holders.
fidelity: PhysX has no bolts in holes or eccentric cams: our model. Square and in line (2.5 mm, 2.5 deg) the edge takes the drawn bolts; a cam open (within 30 deg) lets the head in, closed it stops the shelf 9 mm short however hard it is pushed (nothing breaks). Turned clockwise with the head in, a cam draws the joint shut by 180 deg. A screwdriver tip within 2 mm of a cam turns it. Real sizes (Minifix-type, B = 24 mm); the side cut to 12 cm tall so the hands clear it. Boxes; friction 0.4-1.0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the hands move over the screwdrivers' holders and the shelf but pick nothing up; the cams are not turned); demo: 1.0 (success at step 1,126)
